name: simrelay-mcp
description: List SIMs (grouped by team, with lock status), lock/release them, fetch SMS history, and stream or synchronously wait for incoming SMS via SimRelay.
long_description:
## SimRelay for AI agents

This extension lets an AI assistant work with your SimRelay account:

- List every SIM you can access, **grouped by team**, with lock status (unlocked, or locked by whom and until when) and per-organization alias
- Lock a SIM before reading its messages so other agents/users can't interfere
- Release the lock when done (idempotent)
- Read paginated SMS history for any SIM
- **Synchronously wait** for the next incoming SMS — perfect for OTP-style workflows; the message arrives directly in the conversation
- Subscribe to a real-time WebSocket stream and pull the most recent N buffered messages on demand

## First-time setup

Install the extension. The first time the assistant uses any tool, it will ask you to sign in — just say something like "log me in to SimRelay" and the assistant will run the `simrelay_login` tool, which opens your browser to SimRelay's sign-in page. After you authorize, tokens are saved to `~/.config/simrelay-mcp/tokens.json` (chmod 0600) and refreshed automatically. You can also sign in proactively at any time.

To sign out, ask the assistant to run `simrelay_logout`.

## Authentication

OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE — the same flow as SimRelay's mobile and Chrome extension clients. Credentials never travel through tool arguments and the token file is created with `0600` permissions on macOS/Linux.

## Tools

- `simrelay_login` / `simrelay_logout` — manage SimRelay sign-in
- `list_sims` (read-only) — grouped by team, with lock status and alias
- `lock_sim` (destructive)
- `release_sim_lock` (idempotent)
- `get_sim_messages` (read-only, paginated history)
- `subscribe_to_messages` / `unsubscribe_from_messages` — long-lived WS subscription
- `wait_for_next_sms` — block until the next matching SMS arrives (default 60s, max 300s)
- `get_recent_sms` — last N buffered SMS captured since the server started
- `get_subscription_status` — diagnose WS state and inspect the ring buffer

Full tool reference: see `docs/tools.md` in the source repository.

tools.name: simrelay_login
tools.description: Sign in to SimRelay. Opens the user's default browser to the SimRelay OAuth page; tokens are saved locally and refreshed automatically. Use when the user asks to log in or when other tools fail with 'Not authenticated'.

tools.name: simrelay_logout
tools.description: Forget the saved SimRelay tokens. Use when the user asks to sign out or switch accounts.

tools.name: list_sims
tools.description: List every SIM the authenticated user can access, grouped by team. Each SIM includes id, phone_number, organization-pivot alias, organization, team, type, messages_received_count, and current lock status (unlocked, or locked-by-user with expiry).

tools.name: lock_sim
tools.description: Acquire an exclusive lock on a SIM by its integer hosted_sim_id so other users/agents cannot send or read on it. Locks auto-expire after a server-configured TTL.

tools.name: release_sim_lock
tools.description: Release a previously acquired SIM lock. Idempotent — safe to call even if the lock has already expired.

tools.name: get_sim_messages
tools.description: Retrieve historical SMS messages for a SIM, paginated. Returns normalized messages (id, sim_id, direction, from, to, text, received_at) plus pagination metadata.

tools.name: subscribe_to_messages
tools.description: Open a WebSocket subscription to SimRelay. Each new incoming SMS is delivered to the MCP client as a logging notification (logger=simrelay-sms) so the assistant can react to OTPs and other inbound messages live. Optional sim_id filter.

tools.name: unsubscribe_from_messages
tools.description: Stop the real-time SMS stream. Idempotent.

tools.name: wait_for_next_sms
tools.description: Block until the next incoming SMS arrives (optional sim_id filter) and return its payload directly in the tool result. Best for OTP-style flows where the assistant expects a code imminently. Default timeout 60s, max 300s. Auto-starts the WebSocket subscription if needed.

tools.name: get_recent_sms
tools.description: Return the N most-recent SMS messages captured by the WebSocket subscription in this server's lifetime (ring buffer, capacity 100). Filter-independent. For persisted history use get_sim_messages instead.

tools.name: get_subscription_status
tools.description: Diagnose the realtime subscription: current WebSocket state, channel, active filter, and the latest buffered SMS events. Useful when messages aren't arriving as expected.
